principles: Adapters are declarative and local-only; they normalize evidence but do not run external quantum jobs.
Fail closed on unknown adapter ids, unsupported output versions, missing identity, stale receipts, and digest mismatch.
Quantum pack integration reuses the existing ClaimAdmissibilityPack registry and never creates storage, lifecycle gates, or completion claims.
M2 updates status precisely: M0-M2 implemented; M3-M5 still pending.
drivers: Keep M2 separate from M3/M4/M5 to preserve reviewable Lattice scope.
Preserve existing M0-M1 evaluator behavior and focused smoke coverage.
Avoid circular imports while exposing quantum verifierAdapters in the pack registry.

options.name: descriptor-and-normalizer-only
pros: Smallest M2 slice with deterministic evidence conversion
Keeps lifecycle gate and benchmark work out of scope
Easy to prove with focused smoke
cons: Does not yet enforce quantum gate transitions
Does not execute real solver/verifier commands

options.name: full-domain-pack-now
pros: Would expose gate policy and benchmarks in one larger runtime package
cons: Mixes M2 with M3/M4/M5 and weakens scope control
Harder to review and likely to overclaim scientific correctness

options.name: docs-only-m2
cons: Would leave package registry and smoke unable to prove M2 behavior

rationale: Choose a descriptor-and-normalizer-only M2 because it adds real runtime capability while keeping lifecycle policy, benchmark execution, reporting, and scientific/production/Authority claims out of scope.

preMortem.scenario: Quantum pack import creates a circular dependency between pack-framework.ts and quantum.ts.
preMortem.trigger: pack-framework imports concrete quantum runtime while quantum imports pack types.
preMortem.consequence: Build or runtime import fails and registry becomes unreliable.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep quantum exports independent from pack-framework types where possible, or isolate shared descriptor literals to avoid reverse imports.

preMortem.scenario: Adapter normalization accepts weak or mismatched evidence as admissible.
preMortem.trigger: Normalizer copies active identity into receipts instead of checking verifier output identity.
preMortem.consequence: Mismatched hamiltonian/grid/verifier/output evidence can incorrectly advance.
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke must cover mismatched identity and digest after normalization and confirm evaluateQuantumClaim blocks it.

preMortem.scenario: M2 wording implies quantum theory, hardware, solver improvement, production, or Authority validation.
preMortem.trigger: Runtime status/doc text says quantum verifier pack validates results too broadly.
preMortem.consequence: Users may overclaim scientific or deployment correctness from local admissibility checks.
preMortem.mitigation: Boundary booleans and doc status must keep those claims false/pending, with adversarial smoke assertions.

preMortem.scenario: M2 accidentally implements gate policy or benchmark harness.
preMortem.trigger: Adapter descriptor includes lifecycle transition behavior or benchmark execution hooks.
preMortem.consequence: Story scope overlaps M3/M4 and review burden increases.
preMortem.mitigation: Only add adapter descriptors and normalization; checklist excludes transition engine and benchmark files.
